notes_for_us: Two rules point opposite ways here. Simulation says a '+1 speed' game stays P0 and warns that importing P6 is the classic misfile; the shape catalogue says every P6 is a structural law that cannot be overridden. The slide is both a stat grinder and a continuous run, so the two readings differ on the route and nothing in the files breaks the tie.

'1m studs' is ambiguous between a million studs and one metre, and the downstream expansion read it the other way I did — it built a track '1 meter studs' long. There is no field for a dimension and no instruction about resolving abbreviated numbers, so the two systems silently disagreed about the size of the map by six orders of magnitude.

A game thumbnail is a request that looks spatial and is not. The destination list has `metadata` for it, which is right, but the handoff itself has nowhere to record 'this was asked for and deliberately not built', so only this record knows.

notes_for_us: Second prompt in this batch where the user asks for N differentiated zones without naming them. There is still no way to say 'several distinct themed spaces, contents unspecified' — segments needs names, count needs a number, and the request ends up as one sentence of free text.

Trading between players is a spatial requirement with no option. A trade hub is what social-hub becomes here, but nothing in the catalogue is about player-to-player exchange, and it is a staple of this whole genre of Roblox game.

A cave network under mountains hits P2, P3 and arguably CHECK at once and each is genuinely earned. Worth knowing that the cheapest honest route for a very common Roblox premise is three modifiers deep.

The eight named factory areas are emitted as zone segments. They are gated progression zones of one world, not separate maps, so this is not P4.
Whether a factory is an enterable building or an open-topped plot is unresolved. Roblox tycoons are usually open, so it is routed P0; if the machines are meant to be indoors this becomes P3.

notes_for_us: This is the prompt segments was built for and it worked: eight areas the user named, all zones of one world, no P4. The one soft spot is Secret Factory — named but deliberately undescribed, so its shape is null, which is the rule working as written but reads like a gap in the record.

A conveyor line is a directed sequence of processing stations and there is no option for it. path-circulation is about players walking, trigger-task is one station, physics-rig is the reactions. The single most important piece of geometry in this prompt has to be assembled from three rows plus free text.

Nothing in the files helps decide whether a tycoon factory is an interior. It changes the route from P0 to P3, the prompt says 'inside the factory' but Roblox convention is open plots, and 'read for the feature, not the keyword' cuts both ways here.
